OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-11-11

Today's Highlights

OpenCode shipped v2.2.7, headlined by a GitHub Copilot "Auto" model option that lets Copilot's router pick the model per session at the Auto discount, with a graceful fallback when routing fails. Meanwhile, the issue tracker remains dominated by the still-unresolved free tier usage-limit problem (#59387, 346 comments), plus a cluster of v2.2.x regressions touching Plan mode enforcement, Windows console-window flashing, and plugin cache staleness. On the PR side, the team is actively landing background-subagent and desktop/CLI robustness work.

Releases

v2.2.7 — Release page

  • GitHub Copilot Auto model selection (#62997): When your Copilot account has an Auto pool, selecting Auto in the model picker lets Copilot's router choose the model per session at the Auto discount. If routing fails, OpenCode falls back to the account's default chat model.

Hot Issues

  1. #59387 [OPEN] Free tier issues — read this first — The central triage thread for free-tier failures ("usage exceeded," limits that never reset, desktop version gating). At 346 comments it's the highest-traffic open issue; treat as the canonical signal for go-to-market/billing friction.
  2. #60250 [OPEN] Plan mode enforcement broken in v2.2.1 — Plan agent immediately offers to implement edits instead of only planning. Core workflow regression for anyone relying on plan-then-execute discipline.
  3. #62659 [CLOSED] All sessions lost — data dir recreated (2.2.5→2.2.6) — Total transcript loss on upgrade via a schema bootstrap that started fresh. Severity is extreme (permanent data loss), even though now closed — worth verifying the fix in 2.2.7.
  4. #52266 [OPEN] Windows console windows flashing (~1/sec) — Spawns lack CREATE_NO_WINDOW, causing per-second git.exe console flashes. A re-report of prior issues; long-lived Windows platform debt.
  5. #59461 [OPEN] Crash on startup (Error 134 / missing SSE4.2) — New Bun runtime requires SSE4.2, crashing older CPUs on the desktop client. Hardware-compatibility regression.
  6. #49742 [OPEN] Message timestamp toggle missing in CLI v2 — A v1 Ctrl+P capability dropped in v2.0.8. Representative of accumulated v1→v2 feature-parity gaps (8 👍).
  7. #63188 [OPEN] session.move doesn't update project assignment — Moved sessions keep their old projectID, so they stay filed under the wrong project. Data-model correctness bug in the sessions API.
  8. #63075 [OPEN] [FEATURE] Deny rules should carry a message to the model — Deny-rule hits return a fixed Permission denied string with no reason/alternative, unlike the ask flow. Directly affects agent self-correction quality.
  9. #63174 [OPEN] [reproduced] Invalid retry-after-ms overrides valid Retry-After — An empty/negative retry-after-ms yields a 0 ms delay instead of honoring the header, causing aggressive retries. Networking correctness for provider resilience.
  10. #63171 [CLOSED] Turn settles as "succeeded" with zero content — Answer fully trapped in the reasoning channel is recorded as a normal completion. Silent-failure observability gap.

Key PR Progress

  1. #63210 [OPEN] Always run subagents in the background — Removes the background option; every subagent call returns a sessionID immediately. Stacked on #63209.
  2. #63209 [OPEN] Report subagent results to the parent on every idle — Makes background subagents observable beyond the one-shot job observer, enabling interactive/typed-into children.
  3. #63196 [OPEN] Pipe mode on Windows (process daemon) — Adds create_pipe with CREATE_NO_WINDOW, directly addressing the console-flash class of bugs (#52266).
  4. #63208 [OPEN] Stop freezing main process during login shell env probe — Replaces spawnSync env capture with async; fixes startup UI freeze up to 5 s.
  5. #63213 [OPEN] Scope a client MCP connection to one session — Optional sessionID param for client MCP connections; improves isolation for multi-session MCP use.
  6. #63197 [OPEN] Preserve Claude subscription limit errors — Reclassifies plain Error from Claude Agent so limits aren't surfaced as Unknown.
  7. #62729 [OPEN] CLI fails instead of hanging when event stream never opens — Closes #62681; fixes unbounded waits in opencode run / ACP / TUI reconnect loops.
  8. #63152 [OPEN] Update npm installs through their own prefix — Fixes opencode upgrade under fnm/nvm by using the install's own npm rather than PATH npm.
  9. #61299 [OPEN] @-mention files outside the project directory (TUI) — Ports the V1 behavior (#16464) to V2; a frequently requested ergonomics win.
  10. #60767 [OPEN] Handle stream errors without messages — Fixes schema rejection of OpenAI-compatible error events lacking a message field.

Feature Request Trends

  • Model catalog transparency & deployment control: Pin/verify exact model checkpoints and serve specific builds (#41969, #63110).
  • Agent context & permission control: Edit/delete context messages (#7712), and make deny rules explain themselves to the model (#63075).
  • Desktop UX polish: Keyboard-shortcut help overlay (#63190), keep-awake while agents run (#63082).
  • Billing flexibility: PayPal support for Console credits / Go subscriptions (#62639).
  • Internationalization: Speech-recognition language setting on iOS (#56973).

Developer Pain Points

  • Free-tier reliability & billing clarity is the single loudest signal (#59387), compounded by requests for transparent model versions/checkpoints on paid plans.
  • v2.x migration friction: missing v1 CLI capabilities (timestamps), Plan-mode enforcement regressions, and a catastrophic session-data-loss upgrade path (#62659) erode upgrade confidence.
  • Windows platform quality: console-window flashing, stale-path upgrades under fnm/nvm, and older-CPU/SSE4.2 crashes persist across releases.
  • Silent/ambiguous failures: zero-content "succeeded" turns, stale auth state after DELETE /auth, MCP/plugin cache not invalidating, and retry-header parsing bugs all reduce trust in agent outcomes.
  • Subagent & MCP ergonomics: background execution and per-session MCP scoping are the active frontier the team is addressing this week.

  3. #11961 — Harness.close() releases provider resources (CLOSED). Fixes leaked WebSockets/timers keeping Node processes alive after Codex responses. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11961
  4. #11986 — Tool-search ranks read-only tools for read-verb queries (CLOSED). Fixes gmail_read_email not matching "read my email" because the name wasn't in the search document. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11986
  5. #11985 — Codemode wrapper no longer shadows prelude globals (CLOSED). Removes redundant tools/console params that shadowed globalThis definitions. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11985
  6. #11978 — Expand env vars in custom shellPath (CLOSED). Fixes %LOCALAPPDATA%-style paths failing on Windows. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11978
  7. #11998 — Ling 3.x Flash models in ant-ling (CLOSED). Replaces deprecated Ling/Ring 2.6 with Ling 3.0–3.2 Flash; 3.2 adds image input. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11998
  8. #12002 / #12011 — Session catalog, shares, subagents move to Chord stores (CLOSED). Makes export/import/delete include the session list and enables Chord outbox-based sync. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12002 · https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12011
  9. #11990 — Radius session sync adapter prototype (OPEN). Introduces a backend boundary for session backup/restore without coupling to Radius HTTP API. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11990
  10. #12001 / #12005 — llama.cpp default port + simplified setup guide (OPEN). Standardizes on port 9931 and llama serve as the unified entry point. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12001 · https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12005

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #11984 — Redux/Redux-Saga for Pi state management. Proposes an effect-based agent orchestration model; author references a Redux-Saga discussion thread but admits they lack the means to implement it. Early-stage, worth watching for architecture debate. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11984

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Provider authentication breadth: Entra ID/Azure (#12016), Kimi OAuth host migration (#9819), and ChatGPT sign-in context parity (#11021) all point to demand for first-class, non-API-key auth paths.
  • Catalog fidelity: Multiple reports (#10539, #10683, #10812, #11021) that the model catalog diverges from what providers/accounts actually offer — users want live catalogs and loud failures on stale config.
  • Extension ergonomics: npm resolution via main/exports (#9817), Shiki resolution in standalone builds (#12012), and StringEnum typing regressions (#11869) show the extension surface needs hardening.
  • Cache warming reliability: #10956 and #10536 are the same class of bug across custom messages and virtual models; expect a consolidated fix request.
  • Trust/safety defaults: #12023 argues .pi/agents/ should be trust-requiring and that subagent approval gates are model-disableable — a policy discussion likely to grow.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent degradation: Cache warming stopping, default-model fallback, and stale catalogs all fail quietly, forcing users to dig through logs (/session, cache_warming_decision events).
  • Provider compat fragility: Non-standard streaming shapes (Databricks), header/version pinning (Anthropic OAuth, Fable 5.2), and PII redaction edge cases (#11928) consume significant triage effort.
  • Argument parsing resilience: Corrupted Unicode, lone surrogates (#12014), and malformed JSON from models repeatedly break tool calls — users want a repair layer rather than session restarts.
  • Process lifecycle leaks: #11676/#11961 highlight that resource cleanup on harness shutdown was incomplete, affecting embedding and durable workflows.
  • Standalone binary dependency resolution: Extensions depending on packages not bundled with the binary (Shiki) fail at runtime, a recurring packaging complaint (#12012).
  • Small-terminal UX: Footer truncation on narrow/mobile terminals (#12022) remains an unaddressed quality-of-life issue.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-11

1. Today's Highlights

The project shipped v0.27.2 alongside v0.27.2-preview.0 and SDK TypeScript v0.1.32 (bundling CLI 0.27.2), with the Web Shell gaining multi-channel configuration for WeChat, QQ, and Email (QR login, identity display, logout). Meanwhile, security and permission-classification defects dominated issue traffic: multiple P1 reports show the AUTO-mode classifier approving destructive commands (git branch -D) and misreading redirections, with corresponding fix PRs already open.

2. Releases

v0.27.2 — Stable release (release notes pending generation).

v0.27.2-preview.0 — Preview build including:

  • fix(ci): read prettier's full ignore set at the base tip (#16729)
  • fix(cli,core): allow an Agent Host to retry an enrollment

sdk-typescript-v0.1.32 — Bundles CLI 0.27.2 (built from the same branch/ref as the SDK).

Web Shell Channels (highlighted in release notes) — WeChat, QQ, and Email channel configuration, including QR-based login, scan progress, identity display, and logout where the platform supports it (#16736, #16724).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate — no test identified (292 comments). A long-running CI tracking issue that keeps accumulating failures; the volume of comments signals persistent instability in the managed-agent gate rather than a one-off break.

  2. #16672 — Managed Agent gate: HostedExtensionsIT failure on MySQL 8.4 + 11 more (55 comments). Hosted-extension tests failing under harness replacement/cancellation; broad blast radius across the Java SDK full suite.

  3. #8662 — Migrate TUI rendering from ink to OpenTUI (tracking) (36 comments). Major terminal-UX roadmap item; checkpoint notes show implementation waves merged and the gate now on installation/platform acceptance.

  4. #16787 — E2E: tui-agent-loop-parity — approved write then declined one (34 comments). TUI/agent-loop parity regression in an interactive approval flow — directly user-visible behavior.

  5. #16425 — P1: Workflow agent permission approval never renders; run hangs (7 comments). Reproduced on 0.26.6 and 0.26.8; the status bar shows a pending badge but no approval UI appears, deadlocking multi-agent workflows.

  6. #16856 — P1 security: mid-command input redirection hides words from read-only classifier (2 comments). Example: git branch < /dev/null -D main executes -D main while the classifier sees only the prefix — a genuine safety hole in evaluateCommandSafety.

  7. #16496 — AUTO mode classifier told the pending call already ran (5 comments). The transcript echoes the call being classified as a Prior action, distorting approval decisions.

  8. #15660 — Subagents start with huge context (~105k) of unknown origin (6 comments). Parent at 42k vs. subagent at 105k — token accounting and context inheritance need investigation.

  9. #15327 — P1 tracking: run every surface on one agent loop behind experimental.unifiedAgentLoop (4 comments). Architectural consolidation of the agent loop across CLI, Web Shell, and daemon — high leverage for parity fixes like #16787.

  10. #16824 — Model repeatedly misspells project name ("Lulumi" vs "Luminum") after clean reinstalls (3 comments). Persistent long-context/model-quality complaint; tagged model/long-context, suggesting a caching or context-corruption angle.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16857 — fix(permissions): keep the pending call out of the classifier's prior actions. Threads the call id through the scheduler and ACP session so the transcript builder skips the in-flight functionCall. Direct fix for #16496.

  2. #16862 — fix(ci): retry release Docker test suites once on transient failures. Adds a single retry with container cleanup scoped to the job owner; targets release-pipeline flakiness.

  3. #16574 — fix(cli): in-session MCP enable lifts glob exclusions; rate-limit duplicate WS rejection logs. Two operational fixes for qwen serve.

  4. #9417 — fix(cli): fail closed on expanding heredoc bodies in the worktree guard. Unquoted heredoc delimiters let bash expand bodies that the guard stripped as inert — a security-relevant hardening.

  5. #16664 — fix(acp): report max_tokens when output recovery leaves the answer truncated. Surfaces truncation as a stop reason instead of silently resolving the round.

  6. #16607 — fix(cli): bound provider-warning URL sanitizing to the URL authority. Replaces bespoke indexOf heuristics with sanitizeProviderBaseUrl, closing credential-leak edge cases in /status.

  7. #16669 — fix(cli): enable synchronized output on Windows Terminal 1.23+. DECSET 2026 detection includes native Windows and WSL2 build-number paths — reduces TUI flicker.

  8. #16055 — fix(cli): explicit wrap width for static transcript text. Fixes the mid-word breakage/orphaned-character bug reported in #14075.

  9. #16845 — fix(web-shell): admit GitLab as a repository-only channel. Generalizes the channel model beyond GitHub; hides inert DM controls and accepts nested allowlists.

  10. #16811 — test(generated-ui): acceptance evaluation for #14019. End-to-end runs through qwen serve, Web Shell, the bundled Generated UI provider, and Chromium — only the model is replaced.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in this dataset; section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Channel & integration expansion — Outbound platform webhooks via Channel delivery (DingTalk custom robots) with Web Shell configuration and Scheduled Tasks flows (#16751); GitLab channel support landing via PR.
  • Web Shell UX maturity — Model discovery for custom providers with refresh-and-select (#16785), a dedicated centered session-search dialog (#16778), and a stateful "intelligent UI" with native components and isolated HTML visualizations (#14019).
  • Unified agent loop across surfaces — Consolidating CLI, Web Shell, and daemon onto one loop in packages/core (#15327).
  • Real shell parsing instead of hand-rolled models — Replace shell-semantics.ts with tree-sitter-bash / mvdan/sh plus AST attribution (#16604).
  • Performance at scale — Batched GraphQL CI re-check leg for the GitHub channel (#16692).
  • Terminal UX migration — OpenTUI rendering layer tracking (#8662).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Permission-classifier correctness is the top concern. Three separate reports (#16856, #16496, #16497) show AUTO mode either seeing the wrong command text or approving destructive actions inferred from vague goals ("clean up my branch" → git branch -D). The hand-rolled shell model is repeatedly patched and repeatedly bypassed — the push toward a real parser (#16604) reflects reviewer fatigue.
  • Workflow/multi-agent hangs. Approval prompts that never render (#16425) and teammate messages never reaching the leader in ACP mode (#15738) make multi-agent experiments unreliable.
  • CI noise and flakiness. The bot-generated CI issues dominate volume (#14724 at 292 comments, #16672 at 55, #16787 at 34), with several flagged Provisional — main moving past the head before reports are filed. This erodes signal for contributors.
  • Session-state locks. /cd and /branch failing with "response or tool call in progress" even when idle (#12224, #16700) — a recurring class of stale in-flight-state bugs.
  • Context/token accounting opacity. Subagents ballooning to ~105k tokens (#15660) and model-quality drift after reinstall (#16824).
  • Rendering edge cases. Zero-height viewports blanking the virtualized transcript (#16707), static-mode word-wrap orphans (#14075), and Windows Terminal sync-output gaps (#16669) show long-tail TUI polish work is still substantial.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-11-11

Issues: 287 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-11-10 23:14 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-11

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 依然是一个高速运转的项目：过去 24 小时内有 287 个 issue 和 500 个 PR 有更新，但流水线明显不对称——342 个 PR 仍处于打开状态，仅 158 个已被合并/关闭；活跃 issue 198 个，已关闭 89 个。本次有两个版本落地：一个补丁版本（v2026.11.3）和一个 extended-stable 维护性回移版本（v2026.9.37），表明 9 月线仍在双轨维护。活动评估：非常活跃，但以维护为主。评论最集中的条目围绕会话状态完整性、记忆/梦境提升以及更新/迁移失败，说明项目的稳定性风险集中在长生命周期会话和升级路径上，而非核心 agent 执行。

2. 版本发布

v2026.11.3（发布说明）

  • 私有任务结果： 私有子 agent 的完成结果不再进入流式聊天回复（#188490，@fuller-stack-dev）——这对在共享聊天界面旁运行子 agent 的用户是一项隐私卫生修复。
  • 可靠的子任务交接： 父级在取消子任务后可以交接给替代工作，而不会让被取消的子任务悬空。这与长期存在的 #154572 / #194403 子 agent 权限集群相关，值得寻求修复者关注。
  • 未声明破坏性变更或迁移说明。

v2026.9.37（发布说明）

  • 来自已退役的 2026.9 维护线的仅网关 extended-stable 版本，由维护者明确决定发布。包含 2026 年 9 月代码加上关键安全更新、可靠性/性能修复以及新模型支持。2026.9 线的运维者应将其视为最后一站回移版本，并计划迁移到 2026.10/11 线。

注意： 多份报告表明，对于受影响的安装，通往 2026.11.5-beta.1 的修复路径本身也被阻塞（见 #193962、#193157、#144739）。更新可靠性是一个现实的发布就绪问题。

3. 项目进展

本周期关闭/合并（来自可见样本）：

  • #193962（已关闭，P0，ux-release-blocker）： SQLite 头部探测超时修复无法从 2026.10.10 触达——在 25 条评论后关闭；底层更新路径缺陷（#187197 / #187150 谱系）至少已完成分诊。
  • #154572（已关闭，P1）： sessions_spawn 到 claude-cli 子任务失败并报 SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError——一项有意义的子 agent 可靠性关闭。
  • #149631（已关闭）： CI 预检 Node 矩阵上限（121 > 120 个作业）——CI 管道已修复。
  • #134918（已关闭）： 嵌入式 agent 在 gpt-5.6-sol 上出现空/不完整回合——一个长期存在的模型特定可靠性问题已关闭。
  • #175645（已关闭，not-repro-on-main）： NO_REPLY 子 agent 通告被误分类为 empty_response，消耗了回退链。
  • #156898（已关闭，P1）： 用量成本后台刷新 worker OOM。
  • #149221（已关闭）： 控制 UI 因“无活跃工具权限快照”竞态导致的双重渲染。
  • #141115（已关闭）： 主模型 429 终止会话，而非查询回退。

PR 侧可见合并：#191795（网关运维者 Home 对受限访客的隐私保护，安全敏感）、#196893（macOS 重新打开上次选择的 Gateway）、#196901（测试夹具清理）、#196898（Kova 性能评估器 pin）。

推进中的功能（打开的 PR）： 带重连的 A2A 流式传输（#196903）、发布前的内联模板包审查（#196427）、可编辑的待处理聊天模板添加（#196395）、Git 共同作者资料配置（#196867），以及大规模 CI 后端迁移到“Boat”（#193038、#196894、#196904）。

4. 社区热点

  1. #150635 — 27 条评论（打开，P2，“diamond lobster”）：短期召回在 512 条上限处被驱逐，意味着“梦境深阶段”永远不会提升记忆。今日讨论最多的条目；底层需求是持久、有界的记忆，并具备有意义的提升语义——用户希望梦境是可观察且有效的，而不仅仅是一个管道阶段。
  2. #193962 — 25 条评论（现已关闭，P0）：更新路径无法将 SQLite 探测修复送达受影响的安装。反映了用户对成熟安装上自更新可靠性的挫败感。
  3. #123792 — 18 条评论：助手回合在 claude-cli 后端（UI + Android）上双重渲染，Telegram 不受影响。指向 CLI 后端转录持久化通过两条路径写入。
  4. #154572 — 16 条评论（已关闭）：子 agent spawn 到 CLI 支持的子任务快速失败。尽管已关闭，参与度仍高；2026.9.5 上的用户受到严重影响。
  5. #151962 — 15 条评论：“幽灵用户消息”——内部运行时字符串作为用户提示到达模型，但在 transcript_events 中缺失。这是最侵蚀信任的报告：用户看到的转录与模型看到的不一致。底层需求：转录/审计保真度。
  6. PR 侧：#188295（静默 bootstrap 文件跳过警告）带有“diamond lobster”评级，已准备好供维护者查看。

要点： 社区精力集中在会话状态可观测性和信任——记忆提升、转录完整性和更新正确性——而非新的表面功能。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度排序（P0 → P1 → P2）：

P0 / 发布阻塞：

  • #194664：Codex“受保护续接”在会话 Stop 报告无活跃运行时阻塞所有后续消息（2026.11.1）。每条消息在推理前即失败。无关联修复 PR——正在主动阻塞用户。
  • #190563：无法恢复暂停的 Codex 聊天——提供方审查/原生线程不匹配（回归）。需要安全审查；无修复 PR。
  • #193962：（今日已关闭）更新路径被头部探测超时阻塞。

P1：

  • #194403：辅助完成续接使其自身权限失效，导致对话被阻塞（2026.11.1）。
  • #157255：通道超时后回合声明未释放——会话卡住 90+ 分钟。
  • #181459：3.5 GB 的 agent 数据库使启动成为赌博；commit checkpoint expired；嵌入存储 3 次。
  • #91931：预置的 SOUL/IDENTITY/USER 文件导致 bootstrap 自动完成并在首次运行前删除用户的 BOOTSTRAP.md——数据丢失，UX 影响明确。有对应的修复 PR 在途：#196411（保留自定义 bootstrap 引导）。
  • #168101：工具调用后 Retry-After 忽略 maxRetryDelayMs，在整个睡眠期间占用会话通道。

P2，显著集群：

  • 记忆/梦境： #150635（驱逐 vs. 提升）、#138561（活跃记忆召回在升级后静默停止）、#151173（召回再水化锚定在片段上）。
  • 会话完整性 / 消息丢失： #144594（pendingInputs 卡在 interrupted）、#141172（泄漏的 agent.run.started）、#151962（幽灵提示）。
  • 存储膨胀： #143973 —— view_image 在 transcript_events 中持久化完整 base64（1.3% 的事件 = 80% 的字节）。无修复 PR；高杠杆的清理目标。
  • 安全相关： #159230（message_tool_only 搁浅回复恢复会用私有文本重新提示模型并强制发送英文错误 DM；无关闭开关）。打开的修复 PR：#196848（Discord 被移除 DM 发送者仍通过过期绑定运行命令）、#196847（自托管 web 工具重定向被跟随并访问私有网络）。
  • 更新/迁移： #193157（已退役的 agents.defaults.heartbeat 键拒绝 2026.11.5-beta.1）、#144739（2026.9.3→9.4 npm 更新用旧版本针对 schema-17 状态运行）。
  • 性能/空闲 CPU： #192496（20 个 agent 时空闲技能刷新约 100–170% 核心）、#138918（可见 WebChat 导致 macOS WindowServer CPU）。

已存在的修复 PR： #196411（bootstrap）、#196254（父级压缩/回退后生成会话记忆）、#196853（暂停目标仍运行回合）、#196896（流式激增会话工作减少）、#187668（ACP 失败身份保存）、#165805（节点目录列表分页）。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • #138366 —— 让记忆槽所有者通过 MemoryPluginCapability 中的 dreaming 提供方驱动 Dreams 页面。若被处理，可能合理与 v11.3 子 agent 隐私流合并为即将到来的记忆/扩展 API 增量。
  • #192009 —— 显式跨提供方 cron 回退授权。运维者需求高；可能是配置模式新增而非新 UI。
  • #140213 —— 多个策略别名解析到一个配置模型；已有维护者决策包，是近期合并的有力候选。
  • #151980 —— 会话模型 pin 应继承 agent 回退链。直接补充 2026.9 时代的回退修复；实现成本低，运维价值高。
  • #112372 —— sessions_send 的可选 wakeOnReply 延迟完成（本周期已关闭，可能被取代）。
  • #138990 —— 长时间前台 WebChat 运行的可执行检查点/有界让出。
  • #155039 —— 通过同步偏好手动排序团队侧边栏 agent（UI 打磨）。
  • #119294 —— MCP 2.0（无状态规范）迁移跟踪；已关闭但预示未来破坏性变更轨道。

预测： 下一版本可见功能最可能是 bootstrap 保留（#196411）、生成会话记忆谱系（#196254）、暂停目标支出停止（#196853）、A2A 流式传输（#196903）以及模板发布审查（#196427）。梦境/提供方可扩展性是更长的弧线。

7. 用户反馈总结

痛点：

  • 升级焦虑主导情绪。 2026.10.10 上的用户无法触达修复；2026.9.x 上的用户遇到 schema-17 状态不匹配；2026.11.5-beta.1 被已退役配置键拒绝。更新路径是最一致的挫败来源。
  • 记忆是用户最希望信任的功能。 夜间驱逐击败梦境、升级后召回静默停止、3.5 GB 存储表明用户在生产中依赖记忆并感到其不透明。
  • 转录与运行时分歧令运维者担忧。 幽灵提示和双重渲染回合表明审计面与模型实际所见不一致。
  • 大型安装的扩展问题： 空闲时多 agent CPU、多 GB 数据库上长时间启动、转录中 base64 膨胀。

满意信号： P0/P1 的快速分诊（例如 #193962 约 4 天内以 25 条评论关闭）、对已退役 9.x 线的明确维护者支持回移政策，以及稳定的、署名良好的安全 PR 流（#196848、#196847）显示出受维护的安全态势。

不满信号： 若干 P1/P0 条目在数天至数周等待后仍无修复 PR（#194664、#190563、#157255、#181459）；像 #57278、#92473、#112313 这样标记为 stale 的 issue 已开放数月。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告 — 个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态

日期：2026-11-11 | 项目：OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw

1. 生态概览

个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源领域正处于整合与加固阶段：四个活跃项目均已发布重大架构变更（网关统一、monorepo 迁移、插件运行时重构、OIDC 鉴权），目前正在消化由此带来的会话状态、记忆持久性和 provider 兼容性方面的缺陷。迭代速度依然极高——仅 OpenClaw 一个项目在 24 小时内就触及了 287 个 issue 和 500 个 PR——但活动的性质已从新增表面功能转向可靠性、可观测性和升级路径正确性。一个跨项目的一致痛点模式正在浮现，围绕静默失败（消息丢失、路径截断、用户数据被删除、配置误路由）和自更新/迁移完整性，这表明生态的下一个竞争轴心是信任与可运维性，而非原始能力。与此同时，多渠道触达（QQ、飞书、Telegram、XMPP、SimpleX）和本地推理（llama.cpp、MLX）是两条最清晰的扩展方向。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相对同行的优势

  • 生态引力 / 参考地位： 摘要将 OpenClaw 定位为"核心参考"，其功能面（A2A 流式传输、模板包发布、Git 共同作者配置、CI "Boat" 迁移）比同行领先一代。
  • 双轨维护成熟度： 针对已退役的 2026.9 系列提供显式的 extended-stable 回移（v2026.9.37），这是任何同行都未展现的发布工程纪律水平。ZeroClaw 和 QwenPaw 仍处于 GA 前的单轨阶段。
  • 安全态势： 可见且署名规范的安全 PR（#191795 网关操作员隐私、#196848 Discord 陈旧绑定、#196847 web 工具 SSRF）表明存在活跃的威胁审查流程。
  • 绝对速度： 500 PR / 24h 以数量级优势碾压所有同行。

技术路线差异

  • OpenClaw 以网关 + 会话状态为中心，具有显式的 sessions_spawn / 子代理权限模型和"dreaming"/记忆提升流水线。同行正在向类似的网关概念收敛（Hermes #106742 统一网关），但 OpenClaw 走得更远——相应地也更深地陷入了相关债务。
  • 它运行插件/记忆能力 API（MemoryPluginCapability、dreaming provider）——这是 QwenPaw（#8426 extract-plugin）和 ZeroClaw 等同行刚刚开始的形式化。

社区规模对比

  • OpenClaw 的 24 小时 issue+PR 量（787 项）约为 Hermes（100）的 6.5 倍、QwenPaw（53）的 14 倍、ZeroClaw（69）的 11 倍。其评论线程（27、25、18、16、15）是同类中最深的，表明存在庞大且活跃的运维者基础，而非小型维护者驱动的项目。

注意： OpenClaw 的优势是压力下的广度。其 P0 Codex 续接阻塞（#194664、#190563）没有修复 PR——这是规模更小、关闭更快的项目（ZeroClaw、QwenPaw）很可能已经修补的漏洞。OpenClaw 在能力和生态上胜出；在发布就绪度上处于中游。

  • 第三层 — 休眠： IronClaw（0/24h）。在活动恢复前应排除出活跃生态对比。

快速迭代（功能导向）：

  • QwenPaw — 本地引擎栈（#8649/#8647/#8648）、插件提取（#8426）、技能分类（#8178）。Beta 节奏，当日修复关闭。
  • ZeroClaw — OIDC 设备授权、XMPP/SimpleX 渠道、作用域密钥（#12373）。v0.9.0 即将发布。

  • Hermes — 消化统一网关的余波；Telegram 浪潮正在关闭但网关 P1 仍开启。真正处于稳定化中期。
  • OpenClaw — 成熟但背负集中的会话/记忆/更新债务；"维护繁重"的自我评估与数据吻合。

  2. ZeroClaw — PR 上有记录的风险/规模标签、当日 S1 修复。

  4. Hermes — issue 关闭率最强，PR 合并率和 P1 修复覆盖率最弱。

动能判断： ZeroClaw 和 QwenPaw 在其规模下拥有最佳的关闭-开启平衡，最有可能将动能转化为干净的 GA。Hermes 在其 P1 上存在社区能量与维护者修复速度之间最尖锐的落差。OpenClaw 动能最强，但在没有专门稳定化冲刺的情况下吸收它的余量最少。

7. 趋势信号（对 AI Agent 开发者的价值）

从跨项目社区反馈中提炼——对任何在此生态之上或针对此生态构建的人都是可操作的信号：

  1. 信任是新功能。 每个项目的首要投诉都是静默失败——用户消息被删除（Hermes #137652）、附件路径被截断（QwenPaw #8655）、幻影提示（OpenClaw #151962）、图片消息丢失（QwenPaw #8651）、-w 被忽略（Hermes #67458）。Agent 开发者的设计原则： 每一次变更、丢失、重置或截断都必须发出显式的、用户可见的警告和可恢复的产物。静默降级现在是竞争劣势。

  2. 自更新是生态最薄弱的环节。 OpenClaw 无法向受影响的安装交付修复（#193962），Hermes 需要为旧更新器提供兼容垫片（#152008），ZeroClaw 的安装器误选 musl/glibc（#12153），QwenPaw 的 beta 线在升级时回归。从第一天起就构建可降级、垫片支持、幂等的升级器；将更新路径视为一等、经过测试的产品面。

  3. Provider 参数硬编码是反复出现的集成税。 三个 separate 项目因硬编码 temperature（ZeroClaw #12366/#12362）、缺失 reasoning_content（ZeroClaw #12361）、schema additionalProperties（Hermes #148380）和缺失 thinking_param_style（QwenPaw #7990）而遭遇失败。从目录元数据而非内联常量驱动 provider 行为——并将推理强度控制暴露为一等 UX。

  4. 记忆必须可观测、有界且提升诚实。 OpenClaw 的"dreaming 从不提升"（#150635）、3.5 GB agent 数据库（#181459）和静默召回停止（#138561）表明记忆在生产中被使用但不透明。对记忆阶段进行埋点；让驱逐和提升可见；限制并回收存储。

  5. 转录/审计保真度是治理要求。 OpenClaw 的幻影提示和双重渲染报告（#151962、#123792）表明审计面与模型所见出现分歧。对于受监管或需审计的部署，转录必须是基准真相——通过单一路径写入。

  6. 并行 agent 工作流（Kanban、子代理）撞上并发可靠性墙。 Hermes 的两个 P1 Kanban worker 崩溃（#145022、#139029）和 OpenClaw 的子代理权限集群（#154572 谱系）都源于并发下的所有者仲裁和事件循环阻塞。如果你构建多 agent 编排，预先为所有者仲裁和非阻塞持久化工程留出预算。

  7. 本地推理正在成为一等公民。 QwenPaw 的 llama.cpp/MLX/控制台栈是同类中最大的单一路线图押注。预计GPU 感知、自动更新、UI 管理的本地引擎将成为基线期望，而非插件。

  8. 多渠道是可靠性面，而非复选框。 Telegram（Hermes）、QQ/飞书（QwenPaw）、XMPP/SimpleX/Git（ZeroClaw）都产生了大多数集成缺陷——启动竞态（QwenPaw #8669）和静默丢失（#8651）占主导。将每个渠道视为独立测试的适配器，带启动健康探针。

  9. CI 不稳定现在阻塞发布。 ZeroClaw 挂起的 Telegram 测试和间歇性 Anthropic 回退测试（#12350/#12351）被明确列为发布延迟风险。测试隔离和不稳定检测基础设施是发布关键。

给决策者的底线： 生态的能力前沿正在快速推进，但运营前沿——升级、会话恢复、消除静默失败、provider 元数据和 CI 可靠性——是四个活跃项目都在流血的地方。OpenClaw 在平台深度和生态引力上领先，但在下一个稳定版发布前需要一次稳定化冲刺（合并 #196411/#196254/#196853，解决 #194664/#190563）。ZeroClaw 和 QwenPaw 是动能领先者，通往健康发布的路径最干净，而 Hermes 承载着最高的静默数据丢失风险，应在 v0.24.0 之前分诊。IronClaw 处于休眠，排除在外。

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — 2026-11-11 项目摘要

Hermes Agent 展现出高频、稳定的发布节奏，v0.23.1 汇总了自 v0.23.0 以来约 618 个已合并 PR，同时 main 分支上的发布后稳定化工作仍在继续。活动分布均衡：24 小时内更新了 50 个 issue（23 个开放，27 个关闭）和 50 个 PR（43 个开放，7 个已合并/关闭），表明关闭率健康，但开放 PR 队列在增长。今日的主导主题是统一网关（#106742）合并后的余波——一组 P1/P2 级别的会话状态、Kanban-worker 和消息投递缺陷均可追溯至单进程网关架构。次要主题是 Telegram 适配器可靠性（今日大量修复关闭）和插件目录扩展（多个新目录 PR，可能由黑客松驱动）。总体而言，项目功能上在推进，但网关/会话层存在较高的稳定性风险。

  • 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明： 此补丁中无相关文档。但一个相关的开放 PR（#152008）警告称，v0.22.7–v0.23.1 的更新器需要生成的兼容垫片才能接受 monorepo 模块迁移——如果没有根目录的 hermes_state_common.py 垫片，旧更新器会将迁移后的目录树视为降级而拒绝。对于使用旧版更新器的用户，这是一个需要关注的迁移风险。
  • 完整的精选说明推迟至 v0.24.0。

注意： 这是一个汇总版本；各修复的归属应在 v0.24.0 说明发布后从其读取。

  • 恢复缺口——滞留的 unknown 回合（#148778）让用户没有应用内补救手段。
  • 长尾平台摩擦——Telegram 吸收了很大一部分投诉，但也是今日大多数修复的对象（积极的响应性信号）。

观察到的用例：

  • 多设备个人配置可移植性（#20510）。
  • Kanban 驱动的并行 agent 工作流（多 worker）——一种严肃的高级用户模式，现已触及 P1 可靠性极限。
  • 带有输入/状态指示器的长时间聊天会话。

满意度信号： 高缺陷关闭速度（今日关闭 27 个 issue）、点赞驱动的需求（#20510，👍24）以及活跃的黑客松驱动插件生态（众多目录 PR）表明社区参与度高、投入深。

ZeroClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-11

1. 今日概览

ZeroClaw 正处于冲刺 v0.9.0 的紧张预发布阶段，今天开启了版本号升级 PR（#12377），v0.9.0 发布标签也出现在众多 issue 和 PR 中。活动量非常高：24 小时内更新了 19 个 issue 和 50 个 PR，包括 12 个 issue 关闭和 9 个已合并/关闭的 PR——健康的关闭率表明分类响应及时，而非积压累积。今日工作主要围绕三大主题：zerocode OIDC/设备证书认证加固、文档/SEO 基础设施修复（规范 URL、404 处理、rustdoc 目录树的 noindex），以及一组温度硬编码 bug，这些 bug 会导致拒绝 temperature 参数的模型无法工作。然而，PR 队列严重偏向大型、长期运行的 XL 变更（部分自 8 月至 10 月起一直开放），两个 CI 测试稳定性问题（间歇性 Anthropic 回退测试、Telegram 测试挂起）表明基础设施债务可能延迟发布。整体健康度：吞吐量强劲，但发布关键稳定性和审查带宽是需关注的事项。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时内无新发布。然而，PR #12377（chore(release): bump version to v0.9.0）已开启，将工作区从 0.8.7 升级到 0.9.0，涉及 Cargo.toml、26 个路径依赖和 Cargo.lock——v0.9.0 发布在即。

  • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12377

3. 项目进展

今日合并/关闭的 PR（9 个）：

  • #12317 — feat(zerocode)：免配对 OIDC 登录和保存的远程凭据。重大认证 UX 改进：未知客户端现在无需手动复制 bearer token 即可登录远程守护进程。（风险：高，规模：XL）
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12317
  • #12368 — fix(runtime)：停止在心跳决策和模型路由探测中硬编码 temperature（关闭 #12366）。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12368
  • #12328 / #12329 / #12327 — 文档基础设施：跨发布存活的稳定文档 URL、用于裁剪版本的根 404.html，以及 rustdoc API 树 + 错误页面上的 noindex。
  • #12364 / #12370 — docs(zerocode)：每次设备授权均使用 PKCE；设备证书生命周期终止和 JWKS azp 匹配。
  • 其他支持认证和文档工作流的较小文档/配置关闭。

推进功能的显著开放 PR：

  • #12316 — SimpleX 消息频道，支持语音笔记和加密通话（可选启用）。
  • #11847 — 原生 Rust XMPP，可选传统 OMEMO（自 10 月 19 日开放，XL）。
  • #12269 — 配对设备语音设置和 Web 聊天中的浏览器听写/朗读。
  • #12376 — Web 修复：分离的聊天轮次在轮次中途丢失答案。

4. 社区热点

  • #7432 [Tracker] 运行时、仪表盘登录和网关交付 — 16 条评论，讨论最多的条目。长期运行的 v0.9.0 路线图跟踪器，负责 RFC #5574 中剩余的运行时/网关差距。其活跃度确认 v0.9.0 范围是社区的核心关注点。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432
  • #11984 [Feature] 已登录非管理员账户的仪表盘聊天 — 今日在 2 条评论后关闭；“能登录但不能聊天”的差距是 OIDC 部署的明显摩擦点。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11984
  • PR #11847（XMPP/OMEMO） 和 PR #10407（持久会话提示附件，自 8 月 27 日开放） 仍是互动最多的开放 PR，反映对广泛频道覆盖和持久会话状态的持续需求。

底层需求： 用户正推动 ZeroClaw 从“单操作员工具”转向多用户、多渠道部署（非管理员仪表盘用户、XMPP/SimpleX/Telegram、配对设备），认证/交付管道是瓶颈。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度排序：

  1. S1 — #12354（已关闭）：zerorelay 不刷新 TLS 写入 — 中继服务的仪表盘资源挂起直到 300 秒空闲超时；前门资源延迟到达。工作流阻塞。修复已落地（同日关闭）。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12354
  2. S2 — #12366（已关闭）：心跳第一阶段和模型路由探测硬编码 temperature 0.0 — 破坏拒绝 temperature 的提供商/模型。修复 PR #12368 已合并。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12366
  3. S2 — #12362（已关闭）：技能审查 fork 硬编码 temperature: Some(0.3) — 在拒绝 temperature 的 Anthropic 风格模型上导致 HTTP 400；标记 v0.9.0。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12362
  4. S2 — #12357（已关闭）：zerocode 对受限（非管理员）账户在启动时退出 — 配置/日志面板将权限拒绝视为致命错误。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12357
  5. S2 — #12325（已关闭）：文档规范 URL 包含发布目录名 — 每次稳定发布都会移动 1,025 个规范 URL；由 #12328 修复。
  6. S3 — #12351（开放）：Anthropic 服务器回退测试中的间歇性 CI 测试失败 — 不稳定，尚无修复 PR。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12351
  7. S3 — #12350（开放）：Telegram 频道测试在 CI 并行运行时测试中挂起 直到 30 分钟作业超时——尚无修复 PR；CI 风险。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12350
  8. S3 — #12361（开放）：多轮对话在要求助手历史中包含 reasoning_content 的提供商上失败（Reflection AI / Beam）——ChatMessage 缺少该字段；互操作性差距，无修复 PR。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12361
  9. S3 — #12153（已关闭）：install.sh 在安装了 musl 包的 glibc 主机上选择 musl 构建（Ubuntu 24.04）。
  10. S3 — #12347（已关闭）：zerocode 配置写入器可能丢失对 zerocode-config.toml 的并发更新（读-改-写竞争）。

评估： 温度集群和认证 bug 的当日修复速度强劲；两个开放的 CI 不稳定问题是主要残留稳定性风险。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

今日新开启的请求：

  • #12373 — 只写 WebUI 凭据管理和作用域密钥引用（仅操作员密钥目录；作者明确要求在实现前讨论范围）。安全意识强，可能在 0.9.0 之后。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12373
  • #12372 — Git 频道 draft_mode（占位评论代替流式进度）——减少 Git 锻造平台上的评论垃圾；小型，近期次要版本可能实现。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12372
  • #12353 — ZeroCode 和 Web 聊天中每次对话的运行估算成本，复用现有成本账本。低风险 UX 功能；合理的 0.9.x 候选。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12353

对 v0.9.0 的预测： 发布将以认证（OIDC/设备证书/PKCE）、非管理员用户的仪表盘访问和文档基础设施为主——由 #7432、#11984、#12377、#12362、#12368、#12364、#12370 上的 v0.9.0 标签佐证。成本显示和 Git draft_mode 更可能是 0.9.x 后续。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 痛点 — 认证摩擦： 为远程守护进程复制 bearer token 很痛苦；#12317 的免配对 OIDC 登录直接解决了这个问题，#11984 的“能登录但不能聊天”差距让非管理员 OIDC 用户感到沮丧。
  • 痛点 — 提供商兼容性： 多份报告（#12366、#12362、#12361）显示运行非 OpenAI 风格提供商（Anthropic 变体、Reflection AI/Beam）的用户遇到硬编码参数假设——反复出现的集成质量投诉。
  • 用例 — 团队/多用户部署： 非管理员仪表盘账户、zerocode 中的受限主体和只写密钥管理（#12373）表明采用已超越单操作员使用。
  • 满意度信号： 报告的 bug 当日关闭和修复的快速合并表明用户看到响应式维护；范围明确的 issue 报告数量（主要来自 JordanTheJet 等重复贡献者）表明社区参与度高、技术成熟。
  • 不满意度信号： CI 不稳定（#12351、#12350）和长期 XL PR（#10407、#11847、#11869）可能让等待审查的贡献者感到沮丧。

8. 积压关注

长期未答复或停滞的高价值事项，需要维护者关注：

  • PR #10407 — 持久会话提示附件（自 2026-08-27 开放，XL，风险：高）。最古老的主要功能 PR；需要审查/决策。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10407
  • PR #11847 — 原生 Rust XMPP/OMEMO（自 2026-10-19 开放，XL，需要维护者审查）。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11847
  • PR #11869 — 可选任务拥有的 SSH 传输复用（自 2026-10-19 开放，XL）。
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11869
  • PR #11911 / #11868 — 频道工具结果保留和重复工具调用预防（自 10 月 19-20 日开放，XL，风险：高）；#11868 关闭 #11866 但等待审查。
  • PR #12269 — 配对设备语音设置（自 11 月 6 日开放，XL）。
  • Issue #7432 — v0.9.0 运行时/网关跟踪器：发布关键协调项；继续监控验收证据。

底线： ZeroClaw 展现出高速度和出色的 bug 周转，但 v0.9.0 发布取决于清除开放的 CI 不稳定问题，并将维护者审查带宽投入到大型、老化的 PR 队列。

数据来源：github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw — 摘要生成于 2026-11-11。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-11

Issues: 287 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-10 23:14 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-11

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains a high-velocity project with 287 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24 hours, though the pipeline is clearly asymmetric: 342 PRs remain open against only 158 merged/closed, and 198 active issues versus 89 closed. Two releases landed — a patch release (v2026.11.3) and an extended-stable maintenance-backport (v2026.9.37) — indicating ongoing dual-track support for the September line. Activity assessment: very active but maintenance-heavy. The most-commented items cluster around session-state integrity, memory/dreaming promotion, and update/migration failures, suggesting the project's stability risk is concentrated in long-lived session and upgrade paths rather than core agent execution.

2. Releases

v2026.11.3 (release notes)

  • Private task results: private subagent completions are now kept out of streamed chat replies (#188490, @fuller-stack-dev) — a privacy-hygiene fix for users running subagents alongside shared chat surfaces.
  • Reliable child-task handoffs: a parent can hand off to replacement work after cancelling a child without leaving the cancelled child stranded. Relevant to fix-seekers on the long-running #154572 / #194403 subagent-authority cluster.
  • No breaking changes or migration notes stated.

v2026.9.37 (release notes)

  • Gateway-only extended-stable release from the retired 2026.9 maintenance line, published by explicit maintainer decision. Ships September-2026 code plus critical security updates, reliability/perf fixes, and new model support. Operators on the 2026.9 line should treat this as the last-stop backport and plan migration to the 2026.10/11 line.

Note: Multiple reports indicate the fix path to 2026.11.5-beta.1 is itself blocked for affected installs (see #193962, #193157, #144739). Update reliability is a live release-readiness concern.

3. Project Progress

Closed/merged this cycle (from the visible sample):

  • #193962 (CLOSED, P0, ux-release-blocker): SQLite header-probe timeout fix unreachable from 2026.10.10 — closed after 25 comments; the underlying update-path defect (#187197 / #187150 lineage) is at least triaged.
  • #154572 (CLOSED, P1): sessions_spawn to claude-cli children failing with SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError — a meaningful subagent-reliability close.
  • #149631 (CLOSED): CI preflight Node-matrix cap (121 > 120 jobs) — CI plumbing fixed.
  • #134918 (CLOSED): embedded-agent empty/incomplete turns on gpt-5.6-sol — a long-standing model-specific reliability issue closed.
  • #175645 (CLOSED, not-repro-on-main): NO_REPLY subagent announce misclassified as empty_response, burning the fallback chain.
  • #156898 (CLOSED, P1): usage-cost background refresh worker OOM.
  • #149221 (CLOSED): Control UI double-render from "no active tool authority snapshot" race.
  • #141115 (CLOSED): primary-model 429 terminating the session instead of consulting fallbacks.

PR-side merges visible: #191795 (gateway operator Home privacy from restricted guests, security-sensitive), #196893 (macOS reopen last-selected Gateway), #196901 (test fixture cleanup), #196898 (Kova perf evaluator pin).

Features advancing (open PRs): A2A streaming with reconnect (#196903), inline template-package review before publishing (#196427), editable pending-chat template adds (#196395), Git co-author profile config (#196867), and a large CI backend migration to "Boat" (#193038, #196894, #196904).

4. Community Hot Topics

  1. #150635 — 27 comments (OPEN, P2, "diamond lobster"): short-term recall eviction at the 512-entry cap means the "dreaming deep phase" never promotes memories. The most-discussed item today; the underlying need is durable, bounded memory with meaningful promotion semantics — users want dreaming to be observable and effective, not just a pipeline stage.
  2. #193962 — 25 comments (now CLOSED, P0): update path cannot deliver the SQLite probe fix to affected installs. Reflects user frustration with self-update reliability on mature installs.
  3. #123792 — 18 comments: assistant turns double-rendered on claude-cli backends (UI + Android), Telegram unaffected. Points to CLI-backend transcript persistence being written through two paths.
  4. #154572 — 16 comments (CLOSED): subagent spawn to CLI-backed children failing fast. High engagement despite closure; users on 2026.9.5 were badly affected.
  5. #151962 — 15 comments: "phantom user messages" — internal runtime strings reaching the model as user prompts but absent from transcript_events. This is the most trust-eroding report: users see a transcript that doesn't match what the model saw. Underlying need: transcript/audit fidelity.
  6. PR-side: #188295 (silent bootstrap-file skip warning) carries a "diamond lobster" rating and is ready for maintainer look.

Takeaway: community energy is concentrated on session-state observability and trust — memory promotion, transcript integrity, and update correctness — not on new surface features.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (P0 → P1 → P2):

P0 / release-blocking:

  • #194664: Codex "protected continuation" blocks all follow-ups while session Stop reports no active run (2026.11.1). Every message fails pre-inference. No fix PR linked — actively blocking users.
  • #190563: cannot resume paused Codex chat — provider review/native thread mismatch (regression). Needs security review; no fix PR.
  • #193962: (CLOSED today) update path blocked by header-probe timeout.

P1:

  • #194403: helper-completion continuations invalidate their own authority, leaving conversations blocked (2026.11.1).
  • #157255: turn claim not released after lane timeout — sessions wedged 90+ minutes.
  • #181459: 3.5 GB agent DB makes startup a gamble; commit checkpoint expired; embeddings stored 3×.
  • #91931: preseeded SOUL/IDENTITY/USER files cause bootstrap auto-complete and deletion of user BOOTSTRAP.md before first run — data-loss with clear UX impact. Has a corresponding fix PR in flight: #196411 (preserve custom bootstrap onboarding).
  • #168101: Retry-After ignores maxRetryDelayMs after a tool call, holding the session lane for the full sleep.

P2, notable clusters:

  • Memory/dreaming: #150635 (eviction vs. promotion), #138561 (active-memory recall silently stops after upgrade), #151173 (recall rehydration anchors on fragments).
  • Session integrity / message loss: #144594 (pendingInputs stuck interrupted), #141172 (leaked agent.run.started), #151962 (phantom prompts).
  • Storage bloat: #143973 — view_image persists full base64 in transcript_events (1.3% of events = 80% of bytes). No fix PR; a high-leverage cleanup target.
  • Security-adjacent: #159230 (message_tool_only stranded-reply recovery re-prompts the model with private text and force-sends an English error DM; no off switch). Open fix PRs: #196848 (Discord removed-DM sender still runs commands via stale binding), #196847 (self-hosted web tool redirects followed with private-network access).
  • Update/migration: #193157 (retired agents.defaults.heartbeat key rejects 2026.11.5-beta.1), #144739 (2026.9.3→9.4 npm update runs old version against schema-17 state).
  • Perf/idle CPU: #192496 (idle skills refresh ~100–170% core at 20 agents), #138918 (macOS WindowServer CPU from visible WebChat).

Fix PRs existing: #196411 (bootstrap), #196254 (spawned-session memory after parent compact/rewind), #196853 (paused goal still runs turns), #196896 (streaming-surge session work reduction), #187668 (ACP failed identity save), #165805 (node directory listing pagination).

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #138366 — let the memory slot owner drive the Dreams page via a dreaming provider in MemoryPluginCapability. If addressed, this could plausibly pair with the v11.3 subagent-privacy stream into an upcoming memory/extension API increment.
  • #192009 — explicit cross-provider cron fallback authorization. High operator demand; likely a config-schema addition rather than new UI.
  • #140213 — multiple policy aliases resolving to one configured model; has a maintainer decision packet, a strong candidate for near-term merge.
  • #151980 — session model pins should inherit the agent fallback chain. Directly complements the 2026.9-era fallback fixes; low implementation cost, high operator value.
  • #112372 — opt-in wakeOnReply deferred completion for sessions_send (closed this cycle, likely superseded).
  • #138990 — enforceable checkpoints/bounded yields for long foreground WebChat runs.
  • #155039 — manual team-sidebar agent ordering via synced prefs (UI polish).
  • #119294 — MCP 2.0 (stateless spec) migration tracking; closed but signals a future breaking-change track.

Prediction: next-release visible features are most likely bootstrap-preservation (#196411), spawned-session memory lineage (#196254), paused-goal spending stop (#196853), A2A streaming (#196903), and template-publishing review (#196427). Dreaming/provider extensibility is a longer arc.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Upgrade anxiety dominates sentiment. Users on 2026.10.10 cannot reach fixes; users on 2026.9.x hit schema-17 state mismatches; 2026.11.5-beta.1 is refused by retired config keys. The update path is the single most consistent source of frustration.
  • Memory is the feature users most want to trust. Nightly eviction defeating dreaming, silent recall stops after upgrade, and 3.5 GB stores show users leaning on memory in production and feeling it is opaque.
  • Transcript vs. runtime divergence worries operators. Phantom prompts and double-rendered turns indicate the audit surface doesn't match what the model actually sees.
  • Large-install scaling issues: multi-agent CPU at idle, long startup on multi-GB DBs, base64-in-transcript bloat.

Satisfaction signals: rapid triage of P0/P1 (e.g., #193962 closed in ~4 days with 25 comments), an explicit maintainer-backed backport policy for the retired 9.x line, and a steady stream of well-credited security PRs (#196848, #196847) show a maintained security posture.

Dissatisfaction signals: several P1/P0 items lack fix PRs after days-weekly waits (#194664, #190563, #157255, #181459); stale-tagged issues like #57278, #92473, #112313 remain open for months.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived or high-severity items needing maintainer attention:

  • #91931 (P1, diamond lobster, since 2026-06-10): user BOOTSTRAP.md deletion — data loss on first run. Fix PR #196411 exists; reviewers should prioritize it.
  • #112313 (since 2026-07-21, 12 comments): dead-lettered outbound queue entries are permanent and un-clearable. Needs a product decision on TTL/CLI cleanup.
  • #112638 (since 2026-07-22): session.maintenance enforce mode does not bound the store — thread/channel entries bypass all reclaim. Large-install relevance; needs product decision.
  • #92473 (since 2026-06-12): model fallback notice leaking into user-facing channels (internal info disclosure). Fix-shape seems clear but unmerged.
  • #57278 (since 2026-03-29, oldest in view): Telegram bot-photo reply-context attribution — reported conclusion was too strong; still awaiting maintainer resolution.
  • #144594 (platinum hermit): pendingInputs stuck in interrupted with no replay — session-state/message-loss with a clear fix shape.
  • #132767: CLI host omits "assemble-before-prompt" so context-engine systemPromptAddition arrives one turn late; source fix existed (PR #100984) but was closed unmerged — the original PR is worth reconsidering.
  • #143973: base64 image payloads dominating transcript storage — high leverage for large DBs, no fix PR.
  • PR-side:#171315 (Telegram attachment prep hook) has been open ~4 weeks with a security-boundary merge risk and needs proof; #186966 (copy text from Browser panel) and #188295 (bootstrap skip warning) are marked ready for maintainer look.

Overall health assessment: Velocity is healthy and security triage is active, but the project carries concentrated debt in session state, memory durability, and the self-update path. The clearest near-term wins are merging already-reviewed fixes (#196411, #196254, #196853) and resolving the P0 Codex continuation blocks (#194664, #190563) before the next stable cut.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-11 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape is in a consolidation-and-hardening phase: all four active projects have shipped major architectural changes (gateway unification, monorepo moves, plugin runtime rework, OIDC auth) and are now absorbing the fallout in the form of session-state, memory-durability, and provider-compatibility bugs. Velocity remains exceptionally high — OpenClaw alone touched 287 issues and 500 PRs in 24h — but the character of activity has shifted from new surface features toward reliability, observability, and upgrade-path correctness. A consistent cross-project pain pattern is emerging around silent failures (dropped messages, truncated paths, deleted user data, misrouted config) and self-update/migration integrity, suggesting the ecosystem's next competitive axis is trust and operability rather than raw capability. Meanwhile, multi-channel reach (QQ, Feishu, Telegram, XMPP, SimpleX) and local inference (llama.cpp, MLX) are the two clearest expansion vectors.

2. Activity Comparison

7. Trend Signals (Value for AI Agent Developers)

Extracted from cross-project community feedback — actionable signals for anyone building on or against this ecosystem:

  1. Trust is the new feature. Every project's top complaints are silent failures — deleted user messages (Hermes #137652), truncated attachment paths (QwenPaw #8655), phantom prompts (OpenClaw #151962), dropped image messages (QwenPaw #8651), ignored -w (Hermes #67458). Design principle for agent developers: every mutation, drop, reset, or truncation must emit an explicit, user-visible warning and a recoverable artifact. Silent degradation is now a competitive liability.

  2. Self-update is the ecosystem's weakest link. OpenClaw cannot deliver fixes to affected installs (#193962), Hermes needs compat shims for old updaters (#152008), ZeroClaw's installer mis-picks musl/glibc (#12153), QwenPaw's beta line regresses on upgrade. Build downgrade-safe, shim-backed, idempotent upgraders from day one; treat the update path as a first-class, tested product surface.

  3. Provider-parameter hardcoding is a recurring integration tax. Three separate projects hit failures from hardcoded temperature (ZeroClaw #12366/#12362), missing reasoning_content (ZeroClaw #12361), schema additionalProperties (Hermes #148380), and missing thinking_param_style (QwenPaw #7990). Drive provider behavior from catalog metadata, not inline constants — and expose reasoning-effort controls as first-class UX.

  4. Memory must be observable, bounded, and promotion-honest. OpenClaw's "dreaming never promotes" (#150635), 3.5 GB agent DBs (#181459), and silent recall stops (#138561) show memory is used in production but opaque. Instrument memory stages; make eviction and promotion visible; cap and reclaim storage.

  5. Transcript/audit fidelity is a governance requirement. OpenClaw's phantom-prompt and double-render reports (#151962, #123792) show the audit surface diverging from what the model sees. For regulated or audited deployments, the transcript must be the ground truth — write it through a single path.

  6. Parallel-agent workflows (Kanban, subagents) hit concurrency reliability walls. Hermes' two P1 Kanban-worker crashes (#145022, #139029) and OpenClaw's subagent-authority cluster (#154572 lineage) both stem from owner arbitration and event-loop blocking under concurrency. If you build multi-agent orchestration, budget for owner-arbitration and non-blocking persistence engineering up front.

  7. Local inference is going first-class. QwenPaw's llama.cpp/MLX/console stack is the largest single roadmap bet in the cohort. Expect GPU-aware, auto-updating, UI-managed local engines to become a baseline expectation, not a plugin.

  8. Multi-channel is a reliability surface, not a checkbox. Telegram (Hermes), QQ/Feishu (QwenPaw), XMPP/SimpleX/Git (ZeroClaw) all generate the majority of integration bugs — and startup races (QwenPaw #8669) and silent drops (#8651) dominate. Treat each channel as an independently tested adapter with startup-health probes.

  9. CI flakiness now gates releases. ZeroClaw's hanging Telegram tests and intermittent Anthropic fallback test (#12350/#12351) are explicitly cited as release-delay risks. Test-quarantine and flake-detection infrastructure is release-critical.

Bottom line for decision-makers: The ecosystem's capability frontier is advancing fast, but the operational frontier — upgrades, session recovery, silent-failure elimination, provider metadata, and CI reliability — is where all four active projects are bleeding. OpenClaw leads on platform depth and ecosystem gravity but needs a stabilization pass before its next stable cut (merge #196411/#196254/#196853, resolve #194664/#190563). ZeroClaw and QwenPaw are the momentum leaders with the cleanest path to a healthy release, and Hermes carries the highest silent-data-loss risk that should be triaged before v0.24.0. IronClaw is dormant and excluded.

  • #8178 — Nested skill directories (open since 2026-10-11, size/XXL, first-time contributor). Long-running review; risk of contributor attrition.
  • #8234 / #8236 — GBK/CP936 decoding in file tools and Ollama num_ctx context sizing (open since 2026-10-14, both size/XXL). Important correctness fixes for Chinese Windows users and local Ollama users respectively; both under review for ~4 weeks.
  • #8426 — Extract third-party agent into plugins (open since 2026-10-26, size/XXXL). Architecturally significant; needs maintainer direction on merge sequencing.
  • #8479 — Office skills sync with Anthropic (open since 2026-10-28, size/XXXL, first-time contributor). Large diff, under review — worth prioritizing for cross-agent skill compatibility.
  • #8655 — Attachment path truncation regression (no fix PR yet). Highest-priority unassigned item; should gate 2.3.0 GA.

Health assessment: Strong velocity and fast issue turnaround, but the 2.3.0-beta series shows a regression rate that warrants a dedicated stabilization pass before GA. Channel/plugin reliability is the clear investment focus and the local-engine stack is the marquee roadmap initiative.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-11

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in an intense pre-release sprint toward v0.9.0, with a version-bump PR (#12377) opened today and the v0.9.0 release label appearing across many issues and PRs. Activity is very high: 19 issues and 50 PRs updated in 24h, including 12 issue closures and 9 merged/closed PRs — a healthy close rate that indicates responsive triage rather than backlog accumulation. The day's work was dominated by three themes: zerocode OIDC/device-certificate authentication hardening, docs/SEO infrastructure fixes (canonical URLs, 404 handling, noindex for the rustdoc tree), and a cluster of temperature-hardcoding bugs that break models rejecting the temperature parameter. However, the PR queue is heavily skewed toward large, long-running XL changes (several open since August–October), and two CI test-stability issues (intermittent Anthropic fallback test, hanging Telegram tests) signal infrastructure debt that could delay the release. Overall health: strong throughput, but release-critical stability and review bandwidth are the watch items.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. However, PR #12377 (chore(release): bump version to v0.9.0) was opened, moving the workspace from 0.8.7 to 0.9.0 across Cargo.toml, 26 path dependencies, and Cargo.lock — the v0.9.0 release is imminent.

  • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12377

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today (9):

  • #12317 — feat(zerocode): pairing-free OIDC login and saved remote credentials. A major auth UX improvement: unknown clients can now sign in to a remote daemon without manually copying bearer tokens. (risk:high, size:XL)
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12317
  • #12368 — fix(runtime): stop hard-coding temperature in the heartbeat decision and model-routing probe (closes #12366).
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12368
  • #12328 / #12329 / #12327 — docs infrastructure: stable docs URL that survives releases, root 404.html for pruned versions, and noindex on the rustdoc API tree + error pages.
  • #12364 / #12370 — docs(zerocode): PKCE on every device grant; device certificate end-of-life and JWKS azp matching.
  • Other smaller doc/config closures supporting the auth and docs workstreams.

Notable open PRs advancing features:

  • #12316 — SimpleX messaging channel with voice notes and encrypted calls (opt-in).
  • #11847 — native Rust XMPP with optional legacy OMEMO (open since Oct 19, XL).
  • #12269 — paired-device voice settings and browser dictation/narration in web chat.
  • #12376 — web fix for detached chat turns losing their answer mid-turn.

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #7432 [Tracker] Runtime, dashboard sign-in and gateway delivery — 16 comments, the most-discussed item. The long-running v0.9.0 roadmap tracker owning remaining runtime/gateway gaps from RFC #5574. Its activity confirms v0.9.0 scope is the community's central concern.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432
  • #11984 [Feature] Dashboard chat for signed-in non-admin accounts — closed today after 2 comments; the "sign in but can't chat" gap was a clear friction point for OIDC deployments.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11984
  • PR #11847 (XMPP/OMEMO) and PR #10407 (persistent session prompt attachments, open since Aug 27) remain the highest-touch open PRs, reflecting sustained demand for broad channel coverage and durable session state.

Underlying need: users are pushing ZeroClaw from "single-operator tool" toward multi-user, multi-channel deployments (non-admin dashboard users, XMPP/SimpleX/Telegram, paired devices), and authentication/delivery plumbing is the bottleneck.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  1. S1 — #12354 (closed): zerorelay doesn't flush TLS writes — relay-served dashboard assets hang until the 300s idle timeout; frontdoor assets arrive late. Workflow-blocking. Fix landed (closed same day).
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12354
  2. S2 — #12366 (closed): heartbeat phase-1 and model-routing probe hard-code temperature 0.0 — breaks providers/models that reject temperature. Fix PR #12368 merged.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12366
  3. S2 — #12362 (closed): skill review fork hardcodes temperature: Some(0.3) — HTTP 400 on Anthropic-style models rejecting temperature; v0.9.0-labeled.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12362
  4. S2 — #12357 (closed): zerocode exits at startup for limited (non-admin) accounts — config/logs panes treat a permission refusal as fatal.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12357
  5. S2 — #12325 (closed): docs canonical URLs name the release dir — every stable release moved 1,025 canonical URLs; fixed by #12328.
  6. S3 — #12351 (open): intermittent CI test failure in Anthropic server fallback test — flaky, no fix PR yet.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12351
  7. S3 — #12350 (open): Telegram channel tests hang in CI Parallel Runtime Test until the 30-minute job timeout — no fix PR yet; CI risk.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12350
  8. S3 — #12361 (open): multi-turn fails with providers requiring reasoning_content in assistant history (Reflection AI / Beam) — ChatMessage lacks the field; interoperability gap, no fix PR.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12361
  9. S3 — #12153 (closed): install.sh picks musl build on glibc hosts with the musl package installed (Ubuntu 24.04).
  10. S3 — #12347 (closed): zerocode config writers can drop concurrent updates to zerocode-config.toml (read-modify-write race).

Assessment: strong same-day fix velocity on the temperature cluster and auth bugs; the two open CI flakiness issues are the main residual stability risk.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

New requests opened today:

  • #12373 — Write-only WebUI credential management and scoped secret references (operator-only secrets catalog; author explicitly asks for scope discussion before implementation). Security-conscious, likely post-0.9.0.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12373
  • #12372 — Git channel draft_mode (placeholder comment instead of streaming progress) — reduces comment spam on Git forges; small, plausible for a near-term minor release.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12372
  • #12353 — Running estimated cost per conversation in ZeroCode and web chat, reusing the existing cost ledger. Low-risk UX feature; a plausible 0.9.x candidate.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12353

Prediction for v0.9.0: the release will be dominated by auth (OIDC/device certs/PKCE), dashboard access for non-admin users, and docs infrastructure — evidenced by the v0.9.0 labels on #7432, #11984, #12377, #12362, #12368, #12364, #12370. Cost display and Git draft_mode are more likely 0.9.x follow-ups.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Pain point — auth friction: copying bearer tokens for remote daemons was painful; #12317's pairing-free OIDC login directly addresses this, and #11984's "sign in but can't chat" gap frustrated non-admin OIDC users.
  • Pain point — provider compatibility: multiple reports (#12366, #12362, #12361) show users running non-OpenAI-style providers (Anthropic variants, Reflection AI/Beam) hit hard-coded parameter assumptions — a recurring integration-quality complaint.
  • Use case — team/multi-user deployments: non-admin dashboard accounts, limited principals in zerocode, and write-only secret management (#12373) indicate adoption beyond single-operator use.
  • Satisfaction signal: same-day closures of reported bugs and rapid merge of fixes suggest users see responsive maintenance; the volume of well-scoped issue reports (largely from repeat contributors like JordanTheJet) indicates an engaged, technically sophisticated community.
  • Dissatisfaction signal: CI flakiness (#12351, #12350) and long-lived XL PRs (#10407, #11847, #11869) may frustrate contributors awaiting review.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or stalled high-value items needing maintainer attention:

  • PR #10407 — persistent session prompt attachments (open since 2026-08-27, XL, risk:high). Oldest major feature PR; needs review/decision.
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10407
  • PR #11847 — native Rust XMPP/OMEMO (open since 2026-10-19, XL, needs-maintainer-review).
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11847
  • PR #11869 — opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse (open since 2026-10-19, XL).
    • https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11869
  • PR #11911 / #11868 — channel tool-result preservation and repeated-tool-call prevention (open since Oct 19–20, XL, risk:high); #11868 closes #11866 but awaits review.
  • PR #12269 — paired-device voice settings (open since Nov 6, XL).
  • Issue #7432 — v0.9.0 runtime/gateway tracker: release-critical coordination item; continue monitoring for acceptance evidence.

Bottom line: ZeroClaw shows high velocity with excellent bug turnaround, but the v0.9.0 release hinges on clearing the open CI flakiness and getting maintainer review bandwidth onto the large, aging PR queue.
